clue.text: Most important to get a standard quantity

parts.note: par is the standard or normal level, as in golf or 'up to par'
an amount is a quantity of something

explanation.surface: Advice that getting the right standard measure matters above all.
explanation.definitionFit: Paramount describes the thing of supreme concern, ahead of all others.

clue.text: A star rising in the West

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising means the letters of the star word are read upwards, bottom to top

parts.note: a nova is a star that flares suddenly in brightness

explanation.surface: An astronomer spots a star climbing above the western horizon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns NOVA upwards in this down entry. Avon was a county in the West of England, round Bristol and Bath, and has rivers of that name too.
explanation.definitionFit: Avon was a former English county, and a river, found in the western part of the country.

clue.text: Oriental I in Madrid becomes highly respected

indicators.note: becomes signals that the letters turn into something new, a rearrangement of the city with the eastern letter

parts.note: Oriental means eastern, abbreviated E

explanation.surface: A visitor from the East arrives in the Spanish capital and wins great esteem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'becomes' rearranges MADRID with E (Oriental, i.e. eastern) to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To be admired is to be held in high regard or esteem.

clue.text: Antique battle-axe found by the police

parts.note: antique means old
a bill is a medieval weapon, a blade on a long shaft like a halberd

explanation.surface: An old weapon is discovered by detectives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Battle-axe' suggests a fierce woman, but here it is the weapon. The phrase is British slang for the police.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang names the police force by this nickname, as in 'watch out for the coppers'.

clue.text: Mark the absence of the subtonic

parts.note: no means none, an absence of something
te is the seventh degree of the scale in tonic sol-fa

explanation.surface: A music examiner deducts points because the leading note is missing.
explanation.definitionFit: To note something is to mark or observe it.

clue.text: Boxing aficionado who deals in junk

explanation.surface: A dealer in rubbish who is also a fight fan.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading is playful: a scrap is a fight, so a 'merchant' of scraps is a fan of boxing.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrap is a fight and a merchant here a devotee; the usual sense is a dealer in discarded metal and waste.

clue.text: The way things were done in ancient Rome?

definitions.text: The way things were done in ancient Rome?

parts.words: The way things were done in ancient Rome?
parts.note: a Latin phrase meaning method of working, so it is literally how things were done in the language of ancient Rome

explanation.surface: A history question about Roman customs.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase names someone's method of operating, and Latin was the language of ancient Rome.

clue.text: Housing allowance

explanation.definitionFit: Accommodation means lodging or housing, and also an adjustment or concession made to suit someone.

clue.text: Wise man, to get a huge bottle of wine!

explanation.surface: One of the Magi is handed an enormous flagon.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the three Magi traditionally bore this name, which is also a wine bottle holding sixteen standard bottles.

clue.text: Curse the motherland

parts.note: a dam is the mother of an animal, especially a horse
a nation is a country or land

explanation.surface: Someone swears at their native country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'motherland' reads as one word but splits into mother, DAM, and land, NATION.
explanation.definitionFit: Damnation is used as an oath or exclamation of anger, a curse.

clue.text: Constantly on holiday

explanation.definitionFit: As in 'chatting away', it means continuously; it also means absent from home on a trip.

clue.text: Cereal crops are good given wet weather

parts.note: rain is wet weather

explanation.surface: Harvests do well after a rainy spell.
explanation.definitionFit: Grain is the collective term for cereal plants such as wheat and barley.

clue.text: Island producing copper and barium

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
Ba is the chemical symbol for barium

explanation.surface: A Caribbean island that mines metals.
explanation.definitionFit: Cuba is the largest island in the Caribbean.

clue.text: Small vegetable of glossy appearance

parts.note: a leek is an onion-family vegetable

explanation.surface: A little vegetable that has a shiny look.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleek means smooth and shiny, as of well-groomed hair or fur.

clue.text: Take the plunge, but get nothing in return

indicators.note: in places the zero letter within the word for an exchange

parts.note: swop (swap) is to exchange, giving something in return
nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: A risk-taker dives in but gains nothing back.
explanation.definitionFit: To swoop is to dive or plunge down suddenly, as a bird of prey does.

clue.text: Fell, and had a stomach haemorrhage

parts.note: tum is an informal word for stomach
to haemorrhage is to bleed, so had a haemorrhage gives bled

explanation.surface: A medical mishap: someone fell over and suffered internal bleeding.
explanation.definitionFit: Tumbled means fell over, dropped suddenly.

clue.text: Mean to get dope

explanation.definitionFit: Low-down means despicable or nasty; as a noun it is inside information, which is slang 'dope'.

clue.text: Stuffy, bald-headed Cockney

indicators.note: a Cockney speaker traditionally drops the H at the start of words

parts.note: someone bald-headed has no hair on the head

explanation.surface: A Londoner with no hair is rather pompous.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney is the working-class accent of East London, famous for dropping initial H, so HAIRLESS loses its H.
explanation.definitionFit: Airless means lacking fresh air, close and stuffy.

clue.text: Space reserved for soldiers B in coach

indicators.note: in puts the soldiers inside the word for a coach

parts.note: a stage is a stagecoach
OR is other ranks, ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: Seats on a bus held back for troops.
explanation.walkthrough: A stage, short for stagecoach, is a horse-drawn coach running in stages.
explanation.definitionFit: Storage is room set aside for keeping things.

clue.text: Be proud to produce a plan

explanation.definitionFit: Proud can mean sticking out from a surface, so to jut out; the noun is a planned scheme or undertaking.

clue.text: Father looked thunderstruck

parts.note: pop is an informal name for father
eyed means looked at

explanation.surface: Dad stared in astonishment.
explanation.definitionFit: Pop-eyed means goggling with amazement, astonished.

clue.text: In short, a tracheotomy causes pain

indicators.note: in short points to a brief run of letters held within the medical word

explanation.surface: A brief note that a throat operation hurts.
explanation.definitionFit: An ache is a dull continuous pain.

clue.text: Manage to garage stylish motor

indicators.note: to garage is to house a car, so one word encloses the other

parts.note: to cope is to manage
U means upper-class, hence stylish or refined

explanation.surface: Advice on keeping a fancy car under cover.
explanation.definitionFit: A coupé is a two-door car, so a motor in British slang.

clue.text: Part of Ireland which always heartens Maureen

indicators.note: heartens is read as puts into the heart, so the word for always goes inside the name

parts.note: Mo is a short form of Maureen
ay (aye) is an old word for always

explanation.surface: An Irish county that always cheers up a woman called Maureen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartens' looks like cheers but places AY in the heart of MO. Mayo is a county in the west of Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Mayo is a county on Ireland's western coast.

clue.text: Stern looks from both sides

indicators.note: from both sides means the word reads the same forwards and backwards

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: Someone gives severe glances in every direction.
explanation.definitionFit: The poop is the stern of a ship, its raised rear deck.

clue.text: In Kyoto fungus could well accompany it

definitions.text: In Kyoto fungus could well accompany it

indicators.note: in signals letters held within the Japanese place name and the next word

explanation.surface: A Japanese dish of mushrooms might well be served with bean curd.
explanation.definitionFit: Tofu is bean curd, a Japanese staple that mushrooms might well be served with.

clue.text: Explicitly but verbosely expressed

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means plainly or directly, and read literally it suggests something said with many words.

clue.text: Displayed a splendid picnic

explanation.definitionFit: Spread out means laid out for view; a spread is a lavish meal, here one taken out of doors.
